headline: Clouds are visible reminders that nothing in nature stays still
universal_truth: What seems solid is often just gathered particles waiting to disperse
fun_facts: The average cumulus cloud weighs about 1.1 million pounds—yet floats because air below is even denser
A single thunderstorm can contain enough water vapor to fill an Olympic swimming pool every second
There are over 100 different types of clouds classified by meteorologists
discussion_questions: What 'clouds' in your life looked solid but turned out to be temporary?
How does knowing something is impermanent change how you experience it?
What would you do differently if you truly believed everything passes?

hook.script: Look up. Those clouds drifting by are actually flying rivers—some holding more water than flows through the Amazon. They seem so weightless, yet a single cloud can weigh over a million pounds. How is that possible?

cliff.script: A million-pound cloud floating in the sky seems impossible. We're told heavy things fall. So what's keeping all that water suspended above us?
cliff.prompt: Why don't clouds fall to the ground?

options.text: The water droplets are incredibly small and light
options.response: Yes! Each droplet is so tiny that air resistance keeps it suspended.

options.text: Warm air pushes them up constantly
options.response: Updrafts do help, but there's a simpler reason...

fact1.title: Million-Pound Floaters
fact1.script: That fluffy cumulus cloud overhead weighs about 1.1 million pounds. But each water droplet is just 0.02 millimeters across—so small that air molecules bouncing around can keep them suspended. It's like dust floating in a sunbeam.

fact2.title: Sky Rivers
fact2.script: Atmospheric rivers—long, narrow bands of water vapor—can carry 15 times more water than the Mississippi River. These invisible rivers in the sky bring most of the West Coast's water supply.

fact3.title: 100 Cloud Types
fact3.script: Meteorologists classify over 100 different cloud types. From wispy cirrus at 40,000 feet to ground-hugging stratus, each tells a story about what's happening in the atmosphere. Clouds are weather's messengers.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Clouds remind us that even massive things are temporary. They gather, they disperse, they reform somewhere new. Our problems, our joys, our worries—they're all clouds passing through the sky of our lives.

outro.script: That's Day 3. Tomorrow, we'll follow light itself and discover how it travels. Until then, look up—those clouds have stories to tell.

growTrack.title: Perspective - Cloud Watching
growTrack.activity: Spend 3 minutes today watching clouds. Don't analyze—just observe. Notice how they change shape. This simple practice builds your attention muscle and reminds you that everything is in motion.
